summary.one_liner: The official Docker image for the Jenkins continuous integration and delivery automation server, published on Docker Hub as jenkins/jenkins.
summary.what_it_does: Packages a full Jenkins controller in a Docker image, with LTS, latest and versioned tags on Docker Hub. The README covers running it with port 8080 for the web UI and 50000 for inbound TCP agents, persisting data in /var/jenkins_home via a named volume, and setting JVM options through JAVA_OPTS or JENKINS_JAVA_OPTS. It documents extending the image to set built-in executors, install apt packages as root, copy init.groovy.d scripts, and bake in plugins via the jenkins-plugin-cli tool, with update center variables and marker-file-based plugin upgrade controls. It also includes a Docker Compose example pairing Jenkins with a jenkins/ssh-agent container, plus notes on logging, access logs, environment variable substitution in reference config files, and upgrading by pulling a new image.
use_cases: run a Jenkins CI/CD server in a container
set up Jenkins with Docker Compose and an SSH build agent
preinstall Jenkins plugins in a custom image
persist Jenkins configuration and build data across upgrades
connect inbound TCP or SSH build agents to a Jenkins controller
customize Jenkins with init groovy scripts
notable: Official image maintained under the jenkinsci organization, published as jenkins/jenkins on Docker Hub
jenkins-plugin-cli tool for preinstalling plugins from a list file, with configurable update centers
Init groovy hooks via /usr/share/jenkins/ref/init.groovy.d for custom startup configuration
Optional environment variable substitution (${VAR:-default}) in copied .xml, .conf, .properties and .groovy reference files
Plugin upgrade controls using marker files and PLUGINS_FORCE_UPGRADE or TRY_UPGRADE_IF_NO_MARKER
caveats: Bind-mounting jenkins_home to a host folder can cause permission issues; the README recommends a named volume
Plugin manager CLI needs internet access to the default update centers
Changing update center variables does not change the update center the Jenkins runtime uses
